annotation.title_clean: Senate Bill 67: An Act Providing for the Use of Vehicles with Automated Driving Systems on State Public Highways (Montana Automated Driving Act)
annotation.title_en: Senate Bill 67: An Act Providing for the Use of Vehicles with Automated Driving Systems on State Public Highways (Montana Automated Driving Act)
annotation.summary_en: Montana Senate Bill 67 (2025), an enrolled bill allowing vehicles with automated driving systems on state public highways. It defines levels 1–5, permits levels 1–3 outright, and subjects levels 4–5 to Department of Transportation rulemaking limits, with Department of Justice rulemaking and stakeholder consultation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Levels 1-3 automated driving systems may be used on Montana public highways.
Levels 4 and 5 are allowed subject to limits set by Department of Transportation rulemaking.
DOT may restrict commercial automated vehicles during dangerous road conditions, with exemptions for proven capability.
Department of Justice may adopt rules; both departments must consult stakeholders first.
Local governments may regulate traffic but may not discriminate against automated driving system vehicles.
